model: RajagopalLaiUhlrich2023 (opensim-models master; Rajagopal 2016 + Lai 2017 + Uhlrich 2022), 80 Millard muscles in the scaled model; for SO + MocoInverse muscles replaced by DeGrooteFregly2016 (rigid tendon, passive fibre force ignored, active F-L width x1.5), subtalar/mtp/wrist welded
trial: P1 trial slot 13 (data/p1_trial13_sample.mat, index 0), walking, 637 frames @120 Hz

scaling.method: manualScale, uniform per body; factor = trial-mean per-frame marker distance / generic-model distance (pelvis: mean of ASIS width and HJC width; femur: HJC to mid-epicondyles; tibia: mid-epicondyles to mid-malleoli; feet: mean of femur+tibia (CAL-5TH ratio 1.2+ rejected, marker not at the model's MT5 landmark); torso: mid-AC to mid-HJC; arms: AC-EP for the whole arm); mass distribution preserved

ik.procedure:
Three IK passes with marker placement in between (no static trial).

    pass 1: scaled model, generic marker locations, ONLY anatomical markers
            (ASIS, SACR, HJC, epicondyles, malleoli, CAL, 5TH, AC/EP/WR).
    place:  non-fixed markers -> trial-mean body-frame position; epicondyle /
            malleolus pairs widened to the data's separation (midpoint kept).
    pass 2: all markers.
    place:  non-fixed markers again, now from cluster-informed kinematics.
    pass 3: all markers -> the IK used everywhere downstream.
    Fixed (never moved): ASIS, HJC, epicondyle/malleolus MIDPOINTS -- these
    define the model's pelvis, hip, knee and ankle.

id.comparison_frames: all but 12 frames at each end

dynamic_optimization.cost: MocoInverse default: sum of squared controls (muscle excitations + reserves/residuals, weight 1) + sum of squared muscle activations (minimize_sum_squared_activations = true)
dynamic_optimization.muscle_model: DeGrooteFregly2016, rigid tendon, passive fibre force ignored, active force-length width x1.5, fibre damping 0.1, activation dynamics tau_act/tau_deact = 0.010/0.040 s (inherited from the Rajagopal model by ModOpReplaceMusclesWithDeGrooteFregly2016), tanh smoothing b = 0.1

conventions.lab_to_opensim_text: X_os = -y_lab (anterior), Y_os = z_lab (up), Z_os = -x_lab (subject right); no translation
conventions.cop: COP slid along the force line from the plate-origin height z=-0.1746 m to lab z=0 (wrench unchanged)
conventions.moment_sign: OpenSim generalized-force convention: + = ankle dorsiflexion, knee FLEXION (Rajagopal walker knee), hip flexion moment on the child segment
conventions.id_moment_boneid: boneid whole_body_run(trial, p1_params()) right-leg joint_torque_local[:, j, 1] (torque on distal by proximal about the proximal frame's subject-LEFT axis) times [-1, +1, -1] for [ankle, knee, hip]
conventions.moment_arm: OpenSim Muscle.computeMomentArm (= -dL/dq), m; so/dyn_moment = sum_m force_m * moment_arm_m
conventions.group: argmax over crossed joints of mean |moment arm|
conventions.time: t = i/120 s, the trial's mocap clock; SO and dyn series are NaN outside their windows

notes: No static trial in the export: segment scale factors are trial-mean per-frame marker distances over the generic model's; markers were placed by iterating IK + trial-mean body-frame placement (see ik.procedure).
Visual3D's HJC landmarks are 20% wider apart than the scaled Rajagopal hips while ASIS width matches within 3%, so pelvis markers carry ~13-17 mm RMS of systematic error.
Pelvis residual forces/moments are what ID needs to close without RRA; reserves on leg joints are optimal force 1 N m (penalised like a muscle at control 1), pelvis residuals optimal force 100.
SO and MocoInverse use the identical processed model, external loads and 12 Hz-filtered IK, so differences come from activation dynamics + the excitation cost only.

keys.passive_strain_e0: [M] passive_fiber_strain_at_one_norm_force (only matters if passive force were on)

fiber_kinematics.source: values stored are from the MocoInverse solution (study.analyze); the SO side is an AnalyzeTool + MuscleAnalysis on the identical SO setup
fiber_kinematics.so_vs_dyn_grid: SO/MuscleAnalysis 613 samples (AnalyzeTool grid) interpolated onto the 513 MocoInverse mesh times

force_reconstruction.units: max |reconstruction - reported force| over all right-leg muscles and samples of that solver's own grid, N

keys.c{1,2,3}_moment: [T,3] N m, sum force x the rigid moment_arm (same geometry)
keys.compliant_mask_c{1,2,3}: [M] bool, right-leg muscles with a compliant tendon

ladder.c3: all muscles compliant + passive fibre force on

tendon_compliance.ratio_threshold_justification: Zajac (1989) shows the tendon-to-fibre length ratio l_slack/l_opt sets how much tendon stretch changes fibre length and velocity: tendon stretch at F_iso is eps0 l_slack = 0.049 l_slack, so at a ratio of 1 a fully loaded tendon shifts the fibre by ~5% of l_opt (small vs the active f-L width), while the triceps surae (ratio 5.4-6.6) shift by 27-32% of l_opt. Below ~1 a rigid tendon is a good approximation (also the rule of thumb in Millard 2013 / De Groote 2016: compliance matters for long-tendon muscles).
tendon_compliance.tendon_stiffness_note: every muscle has tendon_strain_at_one_norm_force = 0.049 (DGF default; the Rajagopal-Lai-Uhlrich Millard muscles use the default tendon curve, so nothing like the 0.10 Achilles strain some versions use). kT = ln(6)/0.049 = 36.6; normalized stiffness at F_iso = 0.2 kT 6 = 43.9, i.e. k = 43.9 F_iso / l_slack N/m (soleus_r ~957 kN/m at F_iso).

c1.solver: MocoCasADiSolver (CasADi + IPOPT), MocoInverse problem solved through study.solve() so a guess can be set

c2.solver: MocoCasADiSolver (CasADi + IPOPT), MocoInverse problem solved through study.solve() so a guess can be set

c3.solver: MocoCasADiSolver (CasADi + IPOPT), MocoInverse problem solved through study.solve() so a guess can be set

stances.definition: right Fz > 20 N, complete stances in the window

tendon_compliance.work_definition: power delivered to the skeleton P = -F v (v + = lengthening); tendon P = -F dl_T/dt (tendon_velocity output), fibre P = -F v_M along the tendon; positive/negative parts integrated over each complete right stance, mean over stances
